title: [inbox-core 13/22] Recognize the type or target of an untyped Inbox item
body:
**Blocked by:** #1434, #1451
**Model tier:** high

## Context

Model tier rationale: It changes the central decision path of the tick (what happens to an untyped item) and its staleness and fingerprint rules, with a confidence threshold and an AI-driven branch; a wrong detail either loops recomputation or deletes a proposal on the next edit.

An Inbox item without a type is valid ("Add a Linear MCP", a photo of a receipt, a goal with a date). Today the tick (`readTickSnapshot` in `backend/packages/data/src/inbox/inboxTickAction.ts`) resolves the type only from the `type` edge; with no edge it writes a `needsClarification` card with no proposal, no candidates and no AI call (`writeNeedsClarification`), and repeats that on every edit. The product wants the opposite: the assistant works out what the item is, proposes it directly when it is sure, and asks only when it is not.

#1434 builds the model-backed `computeProposal` and registers the tick; #1451 adds the card properties `recognizedTypeId` (text) and `typeCandidates` (json) used here. The `type` relation of an Inbox item is user-owned (`docs/adr/2026-09-10-single-writer-ownership-model.md`), so the tick can never write it; picking a type is the user's action (the replacement route, #1947). Where a type is chosen by a user, `typeCandidates` is only read there.

Decision: recognition runs for an untyped item, including every time its text changes (the fingerprint changes), and is the only writer of `recognizedTypeId` and `typeCandidates`. The `type` edge is never written.

Decision: the model returns ranked candidates, each either `{ typeId, confidence }` (an active Inbox item type of the tenant, whose catalog is part of the request) or `{ targetDatabaseKey, confidence }` (one of `areas`, `projects`, `tasks`, `people`, `files`, `events`, `healthRecords`, `companies`, `mcpServers`), with `confidence` between 0 and 1. Candidates with an unknown type id, an inactive type or an unknown key are dropped.

Decision: the threshold is a single constant `RECOGNITION_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.7`, kept in one place so it can be tuned without a schema change.

Decision: at or above the threshold the tick computes the proposal for the best candidate exactly as for a typed item and stores `recognizedTypeId` (type-id candidates only; a direct target is remembered by the stored envelope's target database and needs no extra field). Below it the card is `needsClarification` with a localized `reason` and two to four `typeCandidates` `{ typeId, label, targetDatabaseKey }` taken from the ranked type-id candidates, padded with the first active types in list order when the model gave fewer than two.

Decision: the fingerprint of an untyped item stays `computeInboxFingerprint("", text)`; it never uses the recognized type's emoji, so recognizing does not change the fingerprint and cannot trigger a recomputation loop.

Decision: an item with neither text nor any recognized attachment content (supplied by a later attachment-extraction step once it exists) has nothing to recognize and goes to `needsClarification` without a model call, as today.

## Task

Load `state-writes`, `error-handling`, `ai-gateway` and `testing`.

1. In `readTickSnapshot` replace the early `needsClarification` return for an untyped item with a recognition path: resolve the type as `type` edge, else the existing card's `recognizedTypeId`, else "recognize". When an existing, unlocked card already carries `recognizedTypeId` or a recognized direct target and the fingerprint is unchanged, return without a call. Add `recognition: true` and the active-type catalog (id, name, emoji, processing method, target) to the snapshot and to `ProposalComputationInput`.
2. In `proposalComputation.ts` (#1434) add a recognition mode: an extended response schema with ranked `candidates`, the instruction text, and the filtering of invalid candidates. Return `{ candidates, ...proposal result for the best one }`; a single call serves both the recognition and, above the threshold, the proposal.
3. In `inboxTickAction.ts` apply the threshold. Above: build the envelope as for a typed item (type-id candidate: the type's processing method and target; direct target: `entityKind: "database"` with that database's id), write the card with `recognizedTypeId` (when applicable), and clear `typeCandidates`. Below: write `needsClarification` with `typeCandidates`, `recognizedTypeId` null, no proposal and the localized reason of #1495 when that issue is present.
4. Add `recognizedTypeId` and `typeCandidates` to the tick's `allowedSystemKeys`, and keep the staleness check (`writeTickResult`) comparing the same fingerprint and the same type resolution, so a later edit that does not change the fingerprint never turns a recognized card into `needsClarification`.
5. Tests with a stubbed computation: an untyped item with confidence 0.9 produces a `proposed` card and the `type` edge stays absent; a later unrelated update of the item leaves the card unchanged; confidence 0.5 produces `needsClarification` with two to four candidates; an unknown or archived type id from the model is ignored; a model response with only one valid type gets padded; an item with no text and no content makes no call; a locked card is never recomputed; the tick never writes `Inbox.type`.

## Touches

- backend/packages/data/src/inbox/inboxTickAction.ts (type resolution, recognition path, threshold, allowed system keys)
- backend/packages/data/src/inbox/fingerprint.ts (comment only if needed; behavior unchanged)
- backend/services/semprec-api/src/proposalComputation.ts (recognition mode and candidate filtering)
- backend/packages/data/src/__tests__/inboxTick.test.ts
- backend/packages/data/src/__tests__/inboxTickProposal.test.ts
- backend/services/semprec-api/src/__tests__/proposalComputation.test.ts

## Scope

### In scope

- Recognition of an untyped item, the confidence threshold, the two outcomes and the unchanged-fingerprint rule.

### Out of scope

- The card properties (#1451), the computation and its context (#1434, #1987) and the reason text (#1495).
- Replacing an item's type from a candidate tile and recomputing (#1947).
- Extracting content from attachments and transcribing voice notes (#1980).
- Creating hidden system types for projects, areas or other direct targets.

## Acceptance criteria

- When an untyped item is recognized with confidence at or above 0.7, then a `proposed` card exists for the best candidate, the item still has no `type` edge, and a later update that does not change the text leaves the card as it is.
- When confidence is below 0.7, then the card is `needsClarification` with two to four type candidates and a reason.
- When the model names a type id that is unknown or archived, then it is not offered or used.
- When the item has no text and no content, then no model call is made.
